sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: In the survey, {PERCENT} of small teams said the current plan is too expensive.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: But a cheaper tier could cannibalise the standard plan.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Only if we give it the same features.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: Let's add a starter tier for {PRODUCT} with a five-user limit and no integrations.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: I can live with that.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: My worry with a cheaper plan is that it eats into standard.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Not if the feature set is clearly smaller.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: And {PERCENT} of small teams told us the price is the problem.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: Okay, decision: a {PRODUCT} starter tier, capped at five users, with no integrations.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: Fine by me.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Great.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: We've got two onboarding designs on the table.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: The guided tour is the prettier one, for sure.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: But in testing, the checklist got {PERCENT} more people through setup.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: Sorry, was that {PERCENT}?

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: Then we go with the checklist.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: Okay, data wins.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: The checklist design had {PERCENT} more people complete setup than the tour.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: Wait, {PERCENT}?

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: Even though the tour looks better?

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Even so.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: Checklist it is for onboarding.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: Fair enough.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: Next, the legacy export.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Only {NUMBER} accounts used it last month.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: But one of them is {CLIENT}, and they're big.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: We deprecate the legacy export, but only after we've moved {CLIENT} to the new one.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: That works.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Okay.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: Before we kill the legacy export, remember that {CLIENT} relies on it.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: They're one of just {NUMBER} accounts still using it.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: Fine, it gets deprecated once {CLIENT} is migrated, not before.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: Thanks.
